lesson.menu_desc: Closing a meeting with clear actions, owners and deadlines -- 35 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 9 -- Next Steps
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Juliana dos Santos Morais | Lesson 9 -- Next Steps
lesson.grammar_point: deadlines and future time clauses: by, until, within, as soon as / when + present

listenings.text: I have one routine that I never change. Five minutes before the end of every meeting, I stop the discussion and I say: let us agree on the next steps. Then we go through the action items, one by one. Every action item needs three things: a clear task, one owner, and a deadline. Not two owners, one. And not next week, a real date: by Friday, by the fifteenth. Within one hour after the meeting, I send the list of actions to everybody. And when a deadline is close, I send a short reminder. People sometimes laugh at my routine, but my meetings always have results.

I remember a partnership meeting two years ago. It was a great meeting. Everybody was positive, everybody had good ideas, and at the end we all said: great meeting, let us keep in touch. But nobody agreed on the next steps. Nobody had a task, and nobody had a deadline. A month later, we had a second meeting, and we discussed exactly the same things again, because nobody had done anything. That was a lesson for me. Now, at the end of every meeting, I ask one simple question: so, who is doing what, and by when? It is not elegant, but it works.

Hi Juliana, it is Emma from Vancouver. Thanks for the meeting this morning. I just want to confirm a few things. The event is on the twelfth of November, as we agreed. I need the logo of the chamber by Monday, because the designer is working on the invitation this week. As soon as I receive the logo, I will send you the final version. The early registration price is valid until the end of October. And please keep me posted about the hotel. Let us touch base again next Thursday. Talk to you soon, bye.
